what: RFC 3161 time-stamp tokens over the SHA-256 of three signed cic-primitives release records, obtained from the DigiCert public time-stamp authority on 2026-11-03, before the certificate chain of those records ends on 2026-12-31. A token shows that the digest existed no later than the time it states; it shows nothing about who signed the record or whether the release is genuine.

authority.name: DigiCert public RFC 3161 time-stamp authority
authority.transport_note: plain HTTP (port 443 did not answer from the machine that made the requests); the reply is signed, its integrity does not rest on the transport
authority.terms_note: No terms of use for the public endpoint were found: neither the search nor DigiCert's documentation pages state who may use it or restrict its use; they describe it for code signing. Only a SHA-256 digest, an algorithm identifier, a random nonce and a request for the TSA certificate were sent.

trust_anchor.subject: C=US, O=DigiCert Inc, OU=www.digicert.com, CN=DigiCert Trusted Root G4 (self-signed)

verified_against.source: operating system store, Ubuntu package ca-certificates 20260816ubuntu0.24.04.1, /usr/share/ca-certificates/mozilla/DigiCert_Trusted_Root_G4.crt
https://knowledge.digicert.com/general-information/digicert-trusted-root-authority-certificates, entry DigiCert Trusted Root G4 (self-signed), read on 2026-11-03
verified_against.kind: the publisher's own figures: SHA-256, SHA-1 and serial all equal

trust_anchor.note: The reply carries a cross-signed DigiCert Trusted Root G4 (issuer DigiCert Assured ID Root CA, valid to 2031-11-09) with the same public key. It is NOT used as the anchor; the self-signed root (valid to 2038-01-15) is.

developer.subject: C = HU, O = CentralInfraCore, CN = Gabor Zoltan Sinko
developer.source: carried by each of the three records (release.createdBy.certificate); the three records carry the same certificate

developer-ca.subject: C = HU, O = CentralInfraCore, CN = CIC Developer CA
developer-ca.source: NOT carried by the records; a public certificate taken from the owner's local PKI directory (EEC/CICDeveloperCA/CICDeveloperCA2026.pem). That it is the issuer of the developer certificate is shown by openssl verify, not assumed

source-ca.subject: C = HU, O = CentralInfraCore, CN = CIC Source CA
source-ca.source: carried by each of the three records (cic_countersign.authority.certificate); the same in all three

root.subject: C = HU, O = CentralInfraCore, CN = CIC Root CA
root.source: carried by each of the three records (cic_countersign.authority.root_certificate); the same in all three

cic_chain.note: The CIC certificates are public. They are kept because the Developer CA is in none of the records, and because a later check of 'was this signature made while the chain was valid' needs them with the time of the stamp. They are not a trust anchor for the release (docs/P5-TRUST-MODEL-PLAN.md): they say when the chain ended, not whether it may be believed.
